turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We adopted a rescue dog and she panics in the car. Whines, drools, the lot.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Poor girl, that's very common with rescues. Short positive trips help. Start with just sitting in the parked car with treats, engine off.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Just sitting there? Not even driving?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Exactly. Then engine on, then a drive to the end of the road. Build it up slowly, and end each trip somewhere fun, like the park.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She's always in the boot now.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Some dogs feel safer in a covered crate, where they can't see everything rushing past. Others prefer a harness on the back seat near a person.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'll try the crate. Should I

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Better not right before. A light meal a few hours earlier helps with the drooling and the nausea.
